notes: WebSearch was out of budget for this session, so this part was researched only by opening pages directly: government sites, the two parties' own pages, campaign sites those pages link to, Wikipedia, and the Minnesota Legislative Manual 2025-2026 (https://www.lrl.mn.gov/docs/2025/mandated/251328.pdf, read with ballot/pdftext.py). Candidates with no entry beyond their name were not found on their jurisdiction's own page of current office holders, and no campaign site could be found without a search. For the verifier: (1) Pam Myhra's and Dan Sparks's Wikipedia articles do not mention the 2026 race. Myhra is tied by state, party (Republican) and Burnsville, which House District 55A covers; Sparks by state and by Austin and Mower County, where he is the sitting District 4 commissioner on the county's own page. If that tie is judged too thin, delete their born, offices and past_party entries. (2) The Legislative Manual prints Judge Marttila's name as 'Kristen Martilla', with the seat number (47) of the 4th District beside it; mncourts.gov answered 403 and was not asked again. (3) The manual (early 2025) lists other people as Cottonwood County Attorney and Redwood County Recorder; the counties' own pages today name Nicholas Anderson (appointed May 2025) and Amy Gewerth. (4) co.hubbard.mn.us answered 403 and was left alone. Not found on their bodies' current-member pages: Andrew McFarlane (the manual lists another District 1 commissioner), Nahid Khan, Miranda McKay-Chambers, Shawn Overocker, Kelly Lindstrom (a Woodbury News Net guide says 'Current office: None'), Ashyante Shantell Gill, Marcus Hill, Amanda Holweger, Sara Brisco, Sarah Moore, Rebecca Church (the manual lists another Winona County Attorney), Robert Bushard. The Minnesota DFL's endorsed list names other candidates in Senate 27, Senate 64 and House 55A; the Republican Party of Minnesota's nominees page lists only statewide and congressional candidates.

verifier_notes: Every url re-opened on 2026-10-02 and every finding confirmed (30). Wikipedia's Pam Myhra and Dan Sparks articles cite the Legislature's own 'Legislators Past & Present' records for service and party; neither mentions the 2026 race. Myhra is tied by the state, Burnsville (inside House District 55A) and the Republican label our record also shows; Sparks by the state and by Austin and Mower County, where the county's own page lists him as District 4 commissioner. Both births are kept as the year only. Judge Marttila's entry in the Legislative Manual (PDF page 367) is spelled 'Kristen Martilla', seat 47, 'Appointed January 8, 2024'. Corrected: the Mahnomen County address (moved to mahnomencounty.gov), the wording of how the DFL list links the Wieman and DeMay sites, and the Morrison County source wording.
